diagnostic.offlineHint: Needs Resolve Studio open + external scripting = Local. Cache cleanup still works.

memory.title: Session memory
memory.measuring: Measuring — drift shows up within a minute.
memory.verdictWatch: Resolve is bloating. Reloading the project gives back timeline RAM.
memory.verdictHigh: Session is very heavy. Only a restart gives back VRAM and the Fusion cache.
memory.reloadBody: Saved, closed, reopened: the RAM from stacked timelines comes back and you land on your page. Nothing is lost. Not mid-render.
memory.restartBody: Saved, closed, relaunched on "{{project}}" at the page you're on. Gives back VRAM and the Fusion cache, which no API frees mid-session. Takes a minute or two. Not mid-render.

prefs.title: Resolve settings
prefs.subtitle: Real values read from disk. The scripting API can't write these prefs — applying closes and reopens Resolve.
prefs.applyBody: The project is saved, the current config is backed up, Resolve closes, the prefs are written, then Resolve reopens on "{{project}}". Takes a minute or two. Not mid-render.
prefs.backupsHint: The config from before each apply. You can restore it with Resolve closed.
prefs.restoreDone: Config restored. Relaunch Resolve to see it applied.
prefs.noBackups: No backups — the first apply creates one.

loadAllTimelines.label: Load all timelines on open
loadAllTimelines.where: Preferences ▸ User ▸ Project Save and Load
loadAllTimelines.body: When on, every timeline loads into RAM as the project opens. Blackmagic leaves it off by default so projects with many timelines open fast.

resolveMemory.label: Resolve memory limit
resolveMemory.body: Defaults to 75% of RAM. Lowering it won't speed Resolve up: it hands RAM to other apps — including NetsuRush's AI jobs. Balance it against what else you run.

fusionMemory.label: Fusion memory cache
fusionMemory.body: Share of Resolve's allocation reserved for Fusion (80% max). High = smoother Fusion playback, less RAM for Edit and Color.

gpuMode.label: GPU processing mode
gpuMode.body: Auto already picks CUDA on NVIDIA. Only force it if you see OpenCL selected despite an NVIDIA card.

hwDecode.label: H.264/H.265 hardware decode
hwDecode.body: Offloads decoding to the GPU. Reliable on 8-bit 4:2:0; 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 depend on the card. Turn it off if you see artifacts.

liveSave.label: Live save
liveSave.where: Preferences ▸ User ▸ Project Save and Load
liveSave.body: Saves on every change. The manual recommends it and calls the impact minimal; the slowdowns people report are on network or slow storage. On a local SSD, keep it.

timelineBackups.label: Timeline backups
timelineBackups.where: Preferences ▸ User ▸ Project Save and Load
timelineBackups.body: Periodic snapshots on top of project saves. The first one of the day can drag, the rest go unnoticed.

gpu.title: GPU / CPU / RAM monitor
gpu.saturated: {{what}} maxed out — crash risk. Free it or reload now.
gpu.vramUnreadable: Live VRAM monitoring is unavailable for this driver. Processing remains available.

process.title: Heavy processes (whole PC)
process.noneBlocked: No stuck processes to clean up.
process.killForced: Force close — unsaved work is lost.
process.cleanBody: Frozen programs ("Not responding"). Force close — unsaved work is lost.

watchdog.title: Memory watch
watchdog.idle: Idle — turns on during a render or an encode.
watchdog.lastPurge: {{freed}} returned to the machine ({{count}} tasks lightened).
watchdog.suggestBody: These background tasks hold memory that no amount of freeing gives back. Stopping them is your call.

noise.title: Useless background tasks
noise.subtitle: Updaters, overlays, sync clients — always running, never useful while editing.

cleanup.title: Clean the Resolve cache
cleanup.diskFull: Disk nearly full — Resolve may freeze.
cleanup.confirmBody: {{size}} freed. Close Resolve first. Deleted content, rebuilt as needed:

cachessd.title: Cache on a fast SSD
cachessd.where: Project Settings ▸ Master Settings ▸ Working Folders
cachessd.body: Defaults to the system disk, which already takes the OS load. An NVMe separate from your media disk pays off right away.

playproxy.title: Timeline proxy resolution
playproxy.body: Half or Quarter while editing: four times less GPU work at Quarter on 4K. Exports stay full resolution.

optimizedmedia.title: Optimized media
optimizedmedia.body: Transcodes once to DNxHR, then plays smooth. The real fix for sluggish H.264/H.265 — far more than cache.

effectsheavy.title: Stacked effects and grades
effectsheavy.body: It's the load per timeline that costs, not the number of timelines. Smart cache caches the heavy nodes on its own.

mercurygpu.title: Software rendering engine
mercurygpu.body: Mercury Playback Engine in software mode puts everything on the CPU. Pick GPU acceleration if the card allows it.

hwdecode.title: Hardware decoding
hwdecode.body: Without it, every H.264, HEVC or AV1 frame is decoded by the CPU. This is the first cause of stuttering playback.

previewcodec.title: Preview codec
previewcodec.body: I-Frame MPEG renders fast but plays back poorly; ProRes or CineForm play back well but render slower. The right pick depends on the card and the drive.

cacheotherdisk.title: Cache on the footage drive
cacheotherdisk.body: Cache and media on the same volume fight for the same read head. Separating them costs one setting and is felt immediately.

diskcachessd.title: Disk cache on SSD
diskcachessd.body: After Effects reads its disk cache on every preview. On a slow drive, or on the footage drive, it cancels its own benefit.

diskcacheon.title: Disk cache disabled
diskcacheon.where: Preferences ▸ Memory & Performance ▸ Enable Disk Cache
diskcacheon.body: Unchecked, every preview restarts from scratch as soon as the RAM fills up. It is the quietest time sink in After Effects.

mfrcpu.title: CPU share set too high
mfrcpu.body: After Effects wants about 4 GB per core it uses. Past what the RAM can follow, adding cores slows the render down.

bitdepth.title: 32-bit project
bitdepth.body: 32-bit only serves high dynamic range compositions. Enabled out of habit on 8-bit sources, it costs nothing but time.

degraded.title: NetsuRush extension not connected
degraded.body: Disk caches, free space and Adobe processes remain readable. Purges, settings and proxies require the application open with the NetsuRush extension.

status.panelHint: Open the application, then Window ▸ Extensions ▸ NetsuRush.
status.uxpHint: Premiere Pro {{year}} loads UXP first: if the extension is missing from Window ▸ Extensions, reinstall it and restart the application.

cache.title: Disk caches
cache.subtitle: Purging is only possible with the application closed: writing there while Adobe uses it corrupts its cache database.
cache.noneFound: No cache detected on this machine.
cache.dbWarning: Emptying the cache database forces Adobe to reconform every media file on next launch: this is slow, and no setting speeds it up.
cache.autoSaveWarning: Auto-saves are versions of your work, not a cache: once deleted, they do not come back.
cache.runningHint: The application is open: NetsuRush will close it cleanly, purge, then reopen the project.
cache.confirmBody: {{size}} will be freed. The folders are kept, only their contents go.
cache.confirmRestartTitle: Close the application, purge, then reopen?
cache.confirmRestartBody: The application will be closed (it will offer to save), {{size}} will be freed, then the project will be reopened.

procs.title: Adobe processes
procs.subtitle: Premiere Pro and After Effects leave helper processes alive after closing. Each is small, their sum is not.
procs.protectedTip: Host application is running: killing it would lose the current edit.
procs.killForced: Termination is forced: any unsaved work in that process is lost.

purge.title: Purges
purge.subtitle: Actions run inside the application by the NetsuRush extension.
purge.needsPanel: Requires the application open with the NetsuRush extension (Window ▸ Extensions ▸ NetsuRush).
purge.allCachesWarning: "Everything, disk included" also empties the disk cache: slow to rebuild. After Effects may ask for confirmation in its own window.
purge.qeExperimental: Premiere Pro exposes no official purge API: this call goes through the QE DOM, an undocumented interface that changes between versions. If it fails, the Disk caches section does the same job with the application closed.
purge.compatAeft: After Effects 2020 (17.0) through 2026 (26.x). Since 24.3, “Everything, disk included” also empties the disk cache.
purge.uxpEra: Premiere Pro {{year}}: Adobe moved to UXP, ExtendScript is no longer maintained and its support ends in September 2026. This call may fail silently.
purge.uxpFallback: The Disk caches section above does the same job with no Adobe API at all.
purge.hygieneHint: Acts on the open project and stays undoable inside the application.
purge.confirmHeavy: The disk cache will be emptied: previews will have to be recomputed.
purge.confirmHygiene: Modifies the open project. The operation stays undoable inside the application.

prefs.title: Performance settings
prefs.subtitle: Read and written live by the panel: no closing, no file patched.
prefs.needsPanel: Requires the application open with the NetsuRush extension (Window ▸ Extensions ▸ NetsuRush).
prefs.writeOnly: The application exposes no way to read this setting: its current value is unknown, only writing is possible.
prefs.none: No readable setting in this version.
prefs.applyBody_one: {{count}} setting will be written into the application. The batch is validated as a whole: nothing is half-applied.
prefs.applyBody_other: {{count}} settings will be written into the application. The batch is validated as a whole: nothing is half-applied.

gpuAccelType.label: Render GPU acceleration
gpuAccelType.body: Staying on software rendering while a card is available is a flat loss on every frame.

bitsPerChannel.label: Project bit depth
bitsPerChannel.body: 32-bit multiplies the cost of every frame. Often enabled for no reason on an 8-bit project.

imageCachePct.label: Image cache share
imageCachePct.body: Share of the allocated memory reserved for the image cache.

maxMemPct.label: Maximum memory
maxMemPct.body: Share of the machine's RAM that After Effects allows itself.

mfrEnabled.label: Multi-Frame Rendering
mfrEnabled.body: Adobe resets this setting at the end of every script: it only holds for a render driven from NetsuRush, not as a lasting setting.

mfrMaxCpuPct.label: Multi-Frame Rendering CPU share
mfrMaxCpuPct.body: After Effects wants roughly 4 GB per core: raising this percentage on a RAM-poor machine slows things down instead of speeding them up.

enableProxies.label: Use proxies
enableProxies.body: Global switch: Premiere Pro plays attached proxies instead of the sources.

scratchVideoPreviews.label: Video previews folder
scratchVideoPreviews.body: Putting it on a fast SSD, separate from the footage drive, is the disk setting that pays off most.

scratchAudioPreviews.label: Audio previews folder
scratchAudioPreviews.body: Same logic as video, for a much smaller footprint.

scratchAutoSave.label: Auto-save folder
scratchAutoSave.body: Putting it on a different drive than the project protects against a volume failure.

proxy.title: Attached proxies
proxy.needsPanel: Requires Premiere Pro open with the NetsuRush extension.
